transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep forgetting my appointments and daily health stuff, even when I really try to stay on top of it. It’s getting really frustrating because I want to take care of my heart, but I just can't seem to manage all these new medical routines.
Have you noticed any other problems with your memory or concentration, such as difficulty learning new information or following instructions?

Yes, I really struggle to concentrate when people are giving me instructions. Like when the nurse goes over my pill schedule, my mind drifts off to whether I locked the back door or things at the senior center, and I realize I've missed half of what she said. Even just trying to write down my blood pressure, a bird outside or a random thought will distract me and I'll end up wandering off.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, such as feeling sad, anxious, or irritable, that seem to be happening at the same time as these memory and concentration problems?

I haven't really noticed feeling particularly sad, anxious, or irritable. Mostly, I just feel restless, impatient, and frustrated with trying to keep up with all these medical routines and appointments.
Can you tell me more about when these memory and concentration problems started, and if they seemed to begin gradually or came on more suddenly?

The major trouble keeping up with my medical routines really started about 14 months ago after a mild heart scare when all these new appointments piled up. But if I'm being honest, the restlessness and distractibility have been there my whole life, even back in grade school when my teachers sent notes home because I couldn't sit still or stop talking. It just never caused this much of a problem until now when I had to manage so much.

Can you help me understand how your restlessness and distractibility have changed over time, from when you were in grade school to now, and if there were any periods where these symptoms improved or worsened significantly?

To be honest, those behaviors never really went away; I've always had that "motor" running since I was a kid getting sent home with notes for roaming the classroom. It only became a major, overwhelming problem about a year ago after my heart scare. That's when the sudden flood of strict doctor appointments and daily routines made my restlessness and distractibility impossible to manage anymore.

Have you experienced any significant periods in your life where your restlessness, impulsivity, or distractibility noticeably improved, such as during adulthood before your heart scare, and if so, what factors do you think contributed to that improvement?

I don't really recall any period where those traits went away or got better; I've just always been a very active, "on-the-go" person. It simply didn't cause major problems in my life until that heart scare brought on all these strict medical demands and schedules that I'm now expected to follow.
Can you describe how your restlessness and distractibility have impacted your daily life and relationships, and if there are any situations where you feel more in control of these symptoms?

Because of my restlessness and distractibility, I constantly miss or show up late to my heart appointments, mess up my daily medications, and let folks down at the senior center, which has my nieces really worried about me. I don't really have any situations where I feel in control of it, because it always feels like I have an internal motor running that I just can't turn off.
Can you tell me if you've ever experienced periods of excessive restlessness or fidgeting, especially in quiet environments, and if so, how you've managed those feelings?

Yes, absolutely—especially in quiet places like church or classes where my legs are constantly bouncing, my fingers are drumming, and it feels like a motor is running inside me. I "manage" it by popping up to pace the halls, pretending to check on things in my car, or getting up to straighten things around the house. I just can't sit still and calmly deal with quiet environments.

You mentioned that your restlessness and distractibility have been present since grade school, but can you clarify if these symptoms have been relatively consistent throughout your life or if they have significantly worsened with age, particularly around the time of your heart scare?

They haven't actually gotten worse with age; they've been pretty consistent since I was a kid. It's just that the heart scare a year ago dumped a ton of new appointments and daily routines on me, which suddenly exposed how much I struggle to stay organized. The traits themselves didn't change, but the new demands on me did, making it a major problem for the first time.

Can you confirm that your symptoms of restlessness, distractibility, and difficulty staying on task have been present and relatively consistent since childhood, rather than developing or worsening significantly in adulthood?

Yes, I can absolutely confirm these issues go all the way back to childhood. In grade school, my teachers constantly sent notes home because I wouldn't stay in my seat, talked over everyone, and roamed the classroom instead of working. While those behaviors have been there my whole life, they only started causing major problems recently because of all the new, strict medical routines after my heart scare.
